claims.location: source name, comment[label], comment[data file], comment[fraction identifier]
claims.value: 15 nonempty TMTpro channels across each of 24 RAW fractions; channel 134N empty
claims.evidence: FragPipe_Search/PPCM/PPCM_annotation.txt gives 126 Ctrl1, 127N Ctrl2, 127C Ctrl3, 128N Ctrl4, 128C Ctrl5, 129N Ctrl6, 129C PPCM1, 130N PPCM2, 130C PPCM3, 131N PPCM4, 131C PPCM5, 132N NI1, 132C NI2, 133N NI3, 133C NI4, 134N Empty. PRIDE lists exactly Fr1-Fr24 RAW files. The builder emits 15 x 24 = 360 rows and excludes the empty channel.

claims.value: six controls, five PPCM, four NPCM
claims.evidence: The deposited annotation labels six Ctrl, five PPCM and four NI channels. The paper explicitly reports six organ-donor controls, five peripartum cardiomyopathy patients and four nonperipartum cardiomyopathy patients. Mapping NI to NPCM follows this unique 6/5/4 match; the deposited file does not expand NI. NPCM disease is annotated generically as cardiomyopathy.

claims.location: characteristics[organism], characteristics[organism part], characteristics[material type], characteristics[sex]
claims.evidence: The PRIDE protocol specifies heart tissue from patients and donors. The paper reports left-ventricular myocardial samples and explicitly says all patients in the three groups were female.

claims.value: sample number within each Ctrl/PPCM/NI group
claims.evidence: The deposited channel map gives distinct sample aliases with suffixes 1-6, 1-5 and 1-4. The paper states these are biological replicates and no technical replicates were analyzed. The integer is a within-cohort ordinal, not a donor identifier.
Table 2 gives cohort-level age summaries only, not ages tied to the deposited channel aliases.

claims.location: comment[cleavage agent details], comment[reduction reagent], comment[alkylation reagent]
claims.value: sequential Lys-C and Trypsin digestion after TCEP reduction and chloroacetamide alkylation
claims.evidence: PRIDE sample protocol describes Lys-C digestion followed by overnight Trypsin. It specifies TCEP and CAA. The deposited fragger.params uses stricttrypsin for database-search specificity, distinct from the two preparation enzymes.

claims.location: comment[instrument], comment[proteomics data acquisition method], comment[dissociation method], comment[collision energy]
claims.evidence: PRIDE sample protocol gives Orbitrap Eclipse Tribrid, top-intensity DDA with 3-second cycle time, and HCD 35%. The paper's Methods describe the same experiment; fragger.params data_type=0 is DDA.

claims.location: comment[precursor mass tolerance], comment[fragment mass tolerance], comment[modification parameters]
claims.value: 20 ppm precursor and fragment search windows; fixed Carbamidomethyl C and TMTpro K; variable Oxidation M, protein N-terminal Acetyl, and peptide N-terminal TMTpro
claims.evidence: FragPipe_Search/fragger.params gives both 20 ppm windows, fixed and variable modification entries. PRIDE processing protocol agrees on the modification list.

limitations: The deposited channel map abbreviates the four non-PPCM cardiomyopathy samples as NI1-NI4. Their mapping to the paper's four NPCM cases is supported by the unique cohort counts but is not explicitly expanded in the map.
The paper reports cohort-level ages but not sample-level ages tied to channel aliases; every age is marked not available.
The reconciliation helper reads only the first of the two repeated cleavage-agent columns, so it reports Trypsin missing even though both Lys-C and Trypsin appear in every SDRF row.

A TMTpro search archive was used for the channel map and search settings. The paper's supplementary spreadsheet/PDF download from Europe PMC was incomplete and did not contribute any sample mapping claim.
